purpose: Read a bead word one symbol at a time and distinguish the current state, unread suffix and full-word acceptance.
meaning: A deterministic finite-state machine uses a fixed finite state set and a transition rule for each input symbol. This original two-state machine records whether the processed prefix contains an even or odd number of 1 symbols. A configuration includes the current state and the unread suffix; visiting an accepting state before input ends does not yet decide the whole word.

definition.setting: A two-state deterministic finite automaton reading a fixed eight-symbol binary word from left to right.
conditions: The alphabet is Σ={0,1}, the states are Q={E,O}, and the initial state is E. Each 1 changes parity and each 0 preserves it.
Choose one of the four stated eight-symbol words and a whole processed-prefix length k from zero through eight. Leading zeros remain input symbols.
A configuration consists of the current state and the unread suffix. Equal current states can have different unread suffixes and therefore different future transitions.
E is an accepting state, but acceptance of the selected full word is reported only after all eight symbols have been read. Before that point the input is unfinished.
The parity invariant follows by induction on processed-prefix length: zero symbols contain an even count of 1s; reading 0 preserves the count and reading 1 toggles its parity.
definition.domain_notes: The machine has finite memory in its two states and no writable tape. Its remaining input is part of the configuration. This bounded example does not implement a Turing machine, a universal computer or an undecidability result.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original restricted-family arguments; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Start in state E. A 0 symbol preserves the state, while a 1 symbol swaps E and O. After k whole symbols, qₖ records the parity of the number of 1s in the processed prefix. The configuration is the pair of current state and unread suffix. E is the accepting state, but an eight-symbol word is accepted only when all eight symbols have been read and the final state is E.
grammar.precedence: Read exactly one next input symbol, apply its transition to the current state, then advance the processed-prefix boundary by one.

properties.claim: The state records the parity of 1s in every processed prefix.
properties.conditions: Start at E and use the stated 0/1 transition rules.
properties.derivation: The empty prefix has zero 1s and state E. A 0 preserves both parity and state; a 1 changes both. Induction gives the invariant for every prefix.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent mathematical review pending

properties.claim: The current state does not alone determine full-word acceptance at an unfinished prefix.
properties.conditions: At least one unread symbol remains.
properties.derivation: A later 1 can change parity, so the final state must be read only after consuming the whole word.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent mathematical review pending

prompts.prompt: Why is Even at the start not already an Accepted result?
prompts.answer: No symbols have been read, so the selected full word is still unfinished. Later 1 symbols may change its final parity.

prompts.prompt: Can two configurations share a state and still differ?
prompts.answer: Yes. The same state paired with different unread suffixes can encounter different next symbols.
